text:
ConocoPhillips rose 2.67% today, driven by a sharp jump in global oil prices—world crude hit $123.10 per barrel, up significantly from recent levels—combined with signs that geopolitical tensions in the Middle East may ease. Reports of Qatari-mediated talks between the U.S. and Iran aimed at avoiding resumed American military strikes reduced immediate escalation risk, while tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz continued despite Iranian attacks, suggesting the oil market remains functional despite regional instability.

The stock's broader momentum reflects a strong two-week gain of 5.13%, anchored in the reality that energy prices have stayed elevated and refining margins remain robust. The gap between U.S. oil ($103.37) and world prices ($123.1) is substantial, which typically benefits major refiners when they can move crude through their systems—exactly the kind of environment in which companies like ConocoPhillips profit.
